Palmerston North, New Zealand, Nov. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- SunScout Holding Limited (NYSE American/NYSE Texas: SNSC) ("SunScout" or the "Company"), a clean-technology company developing and commercializing autonomous, solar-powered robotic mowers and related solar energy solutions, announced today that the Company had filed its annual report on Form 20-F containing its audited combined financial statements for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026, with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) on November 16, 2026.

The annual report on Form 20-F can be accessed on the Company’s investor relations website at https://www.snsc.ai/investors or on the SEC’s website at www.sec.gov.

The Company will provide a hard copy of the annual report on Form 20-F containing its complete audited combined financial statements for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026, free of charge, to its shareholders upon request. Shareholders wishing to obtain a hard copy may submit their requests in writing by email to investors@snsc.ai, or by post to the Company’s principal executive office at 112 Kaimanawa Street, Kelvin Grove, Palmerston North 4414, New Zealand.

About SunScout Holding Limited

SunScout Holding Limited is a clean-technology company engaged in the design, development, manufacturing, and commercialization of autonomous, solar-powered robotic mowers and related solar energy solutions. Powered entirely by solar energy through the Company's proprietary deployable solar array ("DSA") technology, SunScout's robotic mowers operate independently of the electrical grid and feature autonomous navigation and AI-powered obstacle avoidance. SunScout also provides solar power development solutions, as well as engineering products and services, including precision fabrication, mechanical engineering, and project management. SunScout's mission is to eliminate reliance on fossil fuels in outdoor maintenance and mobile machinery, beginning with lawn care and expanding into adjacent applications.

For more information, please visit the Company's website: https://www.snsc.ai.

Eligible customers will receive an automatic bill credit beginning November 23

DAVENPORT, Iowa, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Iowa American Water announced today that eligible customers will receive a bill credit beginning Nov. 23, following the company's receipt of additional proceeds from settlements reached with manufacturers of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS).

The latest distribution includes approximately $667,000 in settlement proceeds and accrued interest. The credit is expected to be approximately $9.72 per eligible customer account. The credit amount appearing on individual customer bills may vary based on eligibility and the number of qualifying accounts at the time the credit is applied. This is the fourth bill credit being issued to Iowa American Water customers as part of the settlement proceeds. Customers previously received credits of $9.58 in August 2026, $32.48 in February 2026, and $10.81 in November 2025.

"We are pleased to return these settlement proceeds directly to our customers," said Brad Nielsen, president of Iowa American Water. "This credit provides a tangible customer benefit while supporting our continued commitment to providing safe, clean, reliable and affordable water service across Iowa."

Customers do not need to take any action to receive the credit. It will be applied automatically to eligible accounts and identified on the bill as a credit resulting from Iowa American Water's receipt of settlement proceeds from PFAS manufacturers.

Iowa American Water participated with other water systems across the country in multi-district litigation (MDL) seeking to hold PFAS manufacturers financially responsible for costs related to these compounds. Under the company's PFAS Litigation Universal Surcredit, or PLUS tariff, approved by the Iowa Utilities Commission, eligible settlement proceeds are returned to customers through one-time bill credits after legal expenses are deducted.

This is the latest in a series of PFAS settlement distributions to Iowa American Water customers. The company previously distributed approximately $738,000 in November 2025, approximately $2.19 million in early 2026 and approximately $657,000 in August 2026. With this latest distribution, Iowa American Water will have returned approximately $4.25 million in PFAS settlement proceeds to eligible customers, totaling approx. $62.59 to each qualifying customer account holder.

The bill credit is not based on whether PFAS has been detected in a customer's water supply. Iowa American Water remains committed to meeting all state and federal drinking water standards while proactively addressing evolving PFAS regulations.

PFAS are a group of manufactured chemicals that have been used in consumer products and industrial applications for decades. American Water, along with numerous other water utilities nationwide, participated in MDL proceedings seeking damages from manufacturers of PFAS chemicals. Settlement agreements provide payments over multiple years, allowing utilities to return proceeds to customers as funds are received.

Customers interested in learning more about PFAS and Iowa American Water's water quality efforts can visit iowaamwater.com. Customers can also view annual Water Quality Reports for their local community, which provide detailed information about drinking water quality, testing and compliance with state and federal standards.

About American Water
American Water (NYSE: AWK) is the largest regulated water and wastewater utility company in the United States. With a history dating back to 1886 and celebrating 140 years in 2026, We Keep Life Flowing® by providing safe, clean, reliable and affordable drinking water and wastewater services to approximately 14 million people with regulated operations in 14 states and on 19 military installations. American Water's approximately 7,000 talented professionals leverage their significant expertise and the company's national size and scale to achieve excellent outcomes for the benefit of customers, employees, investors and other stakeholders.

For more information, visit amwater.com and join American Water on LinkedIn, Facebook, X and Instagram. 

About Iowa American Water
Iowa American Water, a subsidiary of American Water, is the largest regulated water utility in the state with approximately 90 dedicated employees working to provide safe, clean, reliable and affordable water and wastewater services to approximately 225,000 people. For more information, visit iowaamwater.com and join Iowa American Water on Facebook

Adjusted EBITDA increased 2% in the fourth quarter and 4% in the full year as a result of continued progress on our margin expansion initiatives, favorable contract mix, and strong program performance.

Cash Flow Summary

In the fourth quarter, Amentum generated $392 million of net cash from operating activities and used $24 million and $303 million in investing and financing activities, respectively. Net cash provided by operating activities was driven by strong cash earnings, disciplined working capital management, and reflects one less pay cycle compared to the prior year quarter. Net cash used in investing activities included $22 million in capital expenditures. Net cash used in financing activities consisted primarily of $287 million in voluntary principal payment on the Term Loan B. As of October 2, 2026, Amentum had $521 million in cash and cash equivalents and $3,574 million of gross debt. With net leverage reduced to 2.7x, Amentum has strengthened its financial position, providing greater flexibility for disciplined and opportunistic deployment.

Share Repurchase Authorization

Subsequent to quarter end, the Company’s Board of Directors authorized the repurchase of up to $500 million of the Company’s common stock. The share repurchase program provides additional flexibility to deploy capital as part of the Company’s disciplined capital allocation strategy.

Backlog and Contract Awards

As of October 2, 2026, the Company had total backlog of $48.3 billion, which includes an approximately $1.5 billion de-booking related to contract changes at NASA, compared with $47.1 billion as of October 3, 2025, an increase of 2.4% driven by $15.0 billion in net bookings and 1.1x book-to-bill. Funded backlog as of October 2, 2026 was $6.0 billion, compared with $5.6 billion as of October 3, 2025, an increase of 8.0%.

Notable Highlights

  • NGA Integrated Campus Support (NICS) – The National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA) awarded Amentum an $800 million ten-year contract to deliver technology-enabled solutions that maximize the performance of critical facilities and systems at NGA Washington. The award builds on Amentum’s successful track record of supporting critical infrastructure for national security missions at NGA and across the U.S. government and its allies across the globe.
  • Navy Integrated Training Environment (NITE) 2 – The U.S. Navy awarded Amentum a new $700 million five-year contract to provide comprehensive operations and engineering solutions for the Navy’s live, virtual, and constructive integrated environment. Under this contract, Amentum will use secure AI and data analytics to enhance maintenance and operations, improve system readiness, and modernize systems for complex training scenarios.
  • Australia Nuclear Submarine Shipyard Program – The Australian Naval Infrastructure (ANI) selected an Amentum-led joint venture as its Capability Partner to support the delivery of a nuclear-powered submarine construction yard in South Australia, providing program and construction management. This ten-year program reinforces Amentum’s position as a trusted industry partner, leveraging its extensive global nuclear experience in waterfront infrastructure, waste management, and regulatory in support of supporting global nuclear capabilities.
  • U.S. Army Germany Site Operations – The U.S. Army awarded Amentum a new $375 million single-award indefinite delivery, indefinite quantity contract with a six-year ordering period to strengthen U.S. Army mission readiness across 21 installations in Germany. Through this award, Amentum will leverage its global expertise and advanced digital solutions to enhance operational efficiency, modernize installation support, and enable mission-critical operations.
  • U.K. Nuclear Infrastructure & Remediation Solutions – The United Kingdom nuclear site operator Sellafield Ltd selected an Amentum-led joint venture as a preferred supplier for the nuclear Projects and Asset Care Execution (PACE) program valued up to $2.8 billion over an initial duration of nine years and an optional six-year extension. Amentum will support spent fuel management and retrievals mission through its full lifecycle capabilities, including engineering and design, installation, plant modification, project management and ongoing asset care. Formal award of the framework agreement will follow when final contractual arrangements are concluded.
  • Navy Counter-Unmanned Systems (C-UxS) – The U.S. Navy awarded Amentum a $145 million single-award indefinite delivery, indefinite quantity contract with a five-year ordering period to support the U.S. Navy’s modernization of advanced counter-unmanned systems through research, development, testing, and integration of next-generation technologies to enhance operational capabilities.
  • Classified Intelligence Awards – Amentum was awarded over $350 million in intelligence contracts, including an award supporting enterprise IT and operational objectives to deliver systems engineering, network and infrastructure support, cybersecurity, and platform integration.

The presentation and discussion of Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA Margin, Adjusted Net Income, Adjusted Diluted EPS, Free Cash Flow, and Net Leverage are not measures of financial performance under Generally Accepted Accounting Principles in the United States (“GAAP”). These non-GAAP measures should be considered only as supplements to, and should not be considered in isolation or used as a substitute for, financial information prepared in accordance with GAAP. Management believes these non-GAAP measures, when read in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with GAAP and the reconciliations herein to the most directly comparable GAAP measures, provide useful information in assessing trends in our ongoing operating performance and may provide greater visibility in understanding the long-term financial performance of the Company. The computation of non-GAAP measures may not be comparable to similarly titled measures reported by other companies, thus limiting their use for comparability.

Adjusted EBITDA is defined as GAAP net income attributable to common shareholders adjusted for interest expense and other, net, provision for income taxes, depreciation and amortization, and excludes the following discrete items:

  • Acquisition, transaction, and integration costs – Represents acquisition, transaction and integration costs, including severance, retention, and other adjustments related to acquisition and integration activities.
  • Amortization of intangibles – Represents the amortization of intangible assets.
  • Divestitures – Represents divestiture gains and losses.
  • Loss on extinguishment of debt – Represents the write-off of debt discount and debt issuance costs as a result of debt modifications.
  • Utilization of certain fair market value adjustments assigned in purchase accounting – Represents the periodic utilization of the fair market value adjustments assigned to certain equity method investments and non-controlling interests based on the remaining period of performance for the related contract.
  • Stock-based compensation – Represents non-cash compensation expenses recognized for stock-based arrangements.

Adjusted EBITDA Margin is defined as Adjusted EBITDA divided by revenues.

Adjusted Net Income is defined as GAAP net income attributable to common shareholders excluding the discrete items listed under Adjusted EBITDA and the related tax impacts.

Adjusted Diluted EPS is defined as Adjusted Net Income divided by diluted weighted average number of common shares outstanding.

Free Cash Flow is defined as GAAP cash flow provided by operating activities less purchases of property and equipment. For fiscal year 2026, Free Cash Flow was $583 million, consisting of $627 million of GAAP cash flow provided by operating activities less $44 million of purchases of property and equipment.

Net Leverage is defined as GAAP total debt (excluding unamortized original issue discount and deferred financing costs) less cash and cash equivalents, divided by last twelve months Adjusted EBITDA, which is a non-GAAP measure. For fiscal year 2026, Net Leverage was 2.7x, consisting of $3,574 million of total debt less $521 million of cash and cash equivalents, divided by the last twelve months Adjusted EBITDA of $1,132 million.

Key Terms

adjusted EBITDAfinancial
Adjusted EBITDA is a way companies measure how much money they make from their core operations, like running a business, by removing certain costs or income that aren’t part of regular business activities. It helps investors see how well a company is doing without distractions from unusual expenses or gains, making it easier to compare companies or track performance over time.
free cash flowfinancial
Free cash flow is the amount of money a company has left over after paying all its expenses and investing in its business, like buying equipment or updating facilities. It shows how much cash is available to reward shareholders, pay down debt, or save for future growth. This helps investors understand if a company is financially healthy and able to grow.
View in glossary
book-to-billfinancial
The book-to-bill ratio compares new orders a company has received (bookings) to the products or services it has invoiced or shipped (billings) over the same period. It matters to investors because a ratio above 1 means demand is outpacing fulfillment and the company may grow revenue or build backlog, while a ratio below 1 suggests slowing demand and possible future revenue weakness — think of it as new customer orders versus what the company actually sold.
indefinite delivery, indefinite quantitytechnical
An indefinite delivery, indefinite quantity agreement is a standing contract that lets a buyer place orders over a set period without committing to exact quantities or delivery dates up front; think of it as a blank check for future purchases within agreed limits. For investors, it signals potential recurring revenue and a longer sales runway because the seller can receive multiple orders, but it also leaves some uncertainty in timing and total sales, so forecasts and valuation must account for that variability.

NEW YORK, Nov. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Ready Capital Corporation (“Ready Capital” or the “Company”) (NYSE: RC) today announced that its Board of Directors (the “Board”) has approved a reverse stock split of Ready Capital’s outstanding shares of common stock at a ratio of one-for-ten (the “Reverse Stock Split”).

One-for-Ten Reverse Stock Split

The Reverse Stock Split is scheduled to take effect at 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on December 7, 2026 (the "Effective Time"). At the Effective Time, every ten issued and outstanding shares of common stock of the Company will be combined into one share of common stock of the Company. The Board also approved a reduction of the Company’s authorized shares of common stock from 500,000,000 to 50,000,000, effective immediately following the Effective Time. Following the Reverse Stock Split, the Company will file articles of amendment so the par value of the common stock will remain $0.0001 per share. Trading in Ready Capital’s common stock on a split-adjusted basis is expected to begin at the market open on December 8, 2026. Ready Capital’s common stock will continue trading on the New York Stock Exchange (“NYSE”) under the symbol "RC" but will be under a new CUSIP number: 75574U820.

As a result of the Reverse Stock Split, the number of outstanding shares of Ready Capital’s common stock as of November 23, 2026, will be reduced from approximately 159,105,053 to approximately 15,910,505. The conversion rate of Ready Capital’s 6.25% Series C Cumulative Convertible Preferred Stock and the change of control share cap of its 6.50% Series E Cumulative Redeemable Preferred Stock will be adjusted proportionately in accordance with their terms. The Reverse Stock Split does not affect the number of outstanding shares of either series, or their liquidation preferences or dividend rates.

No fractional shares will be issued in connection with the Reverse Stock Split. Stockholders otherwise entitled to a fractional share will instead receive cash, without interest, based on the closing price of the common stock on the NYSE on the trading day immediately preceding the date on which the Effective Time occurs, as adjusted for the Reverse Stock Split. The Reverse Stock Split will apply to all of Ready Capital’s authorized and outstanding shares of common stock uniformly and will not affect any record holder’s percentage ownership interest, except for de minimis changes as a result of the elimination of fractional shares. Stockholders of record will receive information from Computershare Trust Company, N.A., Ready Capital’s transfer agent, regarding their stock ownership following the Reverse Stock Split and cash in lieu of fractional share payments, if applicable. WESTPORT, Conn., Nov. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Compass Diversified (NYSE: CODI) (“CODI” or the “Company”), an owner of leading middle market businesses, today issued the following statement in response to comments from ADW Capital Management, LLC (“ADW”):

Compass Diversified is focused on closing the gap between the Company’s market price and our intrinsic value by driving profitable growth, generating cash for balance sheet deleveraging and evaluating opportunities to return capital to shareholders when appropriate. We have engaged extensively with our shareholders, including ADW, on these priorities and our communications have been consistent and comprehensive.

Over the course of 2026 we have made progress against our stated priorities. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, income from continuing operations (GAAP) was $74.2 million.   Subsidiary Adjusted EBITDA (Non-GAAP) increased 11.0% for the nine-month period year over year, excluding Lugano and the divested Sterno Food Service Business. Branded Consumer Adjusted EBITDA increased 21.2% for the nine-month period year over year, excluding Lugano. At September 30, 2026, total outstanding debt was $1.57 billion, down $319 million from December 31, 2025, reflecting continued progress in strengthening our balance sheet, reducing our leverage and enhancing our financial flexibility.

We have initiated multiple asset sale processes as we evaluate opportunities to maximize value across our subsidiary companies. In May, we sold Sterno's Food Service Business for an enterprise value of $292.5 million and used approximately $282 million of proceeds to repay debt. This demonstrates our ability to execute transactions at attractive valuations. We continue to pursue additional subsidiary-level actions designed to reduce leverage and enhance financial flexibility. As we have stated, we are committed to executing value enhancing subsidiary sales, but will not sell high-quality assets below their intrinsic value just to satisfy short-term interests.

In July, we amended our Management Services Agreement (MSA) to further strengthen its alignment with shareholder interests following a thoughtful Board-led review that considered investor perspectives, market practices and pre-existing contractual requirements. We expect the amended MSA to lower 2027 management fees by approximately $19 million to $22 million, and it ties part of the Manager's compensation to relative total shareholder return. The revised framework is lower cost, more performance based and supports CODI's focus on accelerating deleveraging and strengthening financial flexibility.

Collectively, our actions demonstrate our continued commitment to execute against our priorities and reflect a disciplined approach by the Board and management team to enhance long-term shareholder value.

The 2027 Annual Meeting has not yet been scheduled, and CODI shareholders are not required to take any action at this time.

Jefferies LLC is serving as financial advisor, and Squire Patton Boggs (US) LLP and Sidley Austin LLP are serving as legal counsel to CODI.

About Compass Diversified (“CODI”)

CODI has consistently executed its strategy of owning and managing a diverse set of middle-market businesses. CODI leverages its permanent capital base and long-term disciplined approach, maintaining controlling ownership interests in each of its subsidiaries and maximizing its ability to impact long-term cash flow generation and value creation. The Company provides both debt and equity capital for its subsidiaries, contributing to their financial and operating flexibility. CODI utilizes the cash flows generated by its subsidiaries to invest in the long-term growth of the Company and seeks to generate strong returns through its culture of transparency, alignment and accountability.

Non-GAAP Financial Measures

Subsidiary Adjusted EBITDA excluding Lugano and the divested Sterno Food Service Business and Branded Consumer Adjusted EBITDA, excluding Lugano, are non-GAAP financial measures used by the Company to assess its performance. We have reconciled Subsidiary Adjusted EBITDA excluding Lugano and the divested Sterno Food Service Business and Branded Consumer Adjusted EBITDA, excluding Lugano, to Income (Loss) from Continuing Operations. We consider Income (Loss) from Continuing Operations to be the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure to Subsidiary Adjusted EBITDA excluding Lugano and the divested Sterno Food Service Business and Branded Consumer Adjusted EBITDA. The attached schedules should be read together as continuous reconciliations of the applicable non-GAAP measures to their most directly comparable GAAP measures.

We believe that Adjusted EBITDA provides useful information to investors and reflects important financial measures, as it excludes the effects of items that reflect the impact of long-term investment decisions, rather than the performance of near-term operations. When compared to Net Income (Loss) from Continuing Operations, Adjusted EBITDA is limited in that it does not reflect the periodic costs of certain capital assets used in generating revenues of our businesses, non-cash charges associated with impairments and certain cash charges. The presentation of Adjusted EBITDA allows investors to view the performance of our businesses in a manner similar to the methods used by us and the management of our businesses, provides additional insight into our operating results and provides a measure for evaluating targeted businesses for acquisition.

As used in the body of this press release, Subsidiary Adjusted EBITDA refers to the sum of Adjusted EBITDA for the applicable period attributable to each consolidated subsidiary of the Company, disregarding corporate expense, unless the context indicates otherwise. Management uses Subsidiary Adjusted EBITDA to evaluate the operating performance of subsidiaries before corporate expense. Because the measure excludes corporate expense, it does not reflect CODI’s consolidated operating results and should be considered together with the comparable GAAP measure and the other information in this release.

Subsidiary Adjusted EBITDA, excluding Lugano and the divested Sterno Food Service Business, represents Subsidiary Adjusted EBITDA after excluding Adjusted EBITDA (loss) attributable to Lugano and Adjusted EBITDA attributable to the divested Sterno Food Service Business. Branded Consumer Adjusted EBITDA, excluding Lugano, represents Subsidiary Adjusted EBITDA for our branded consumer businesses after excluding Adjusted EBITDA (loss) attributable to Lugano. We believe these measures facilitate comparison of the operating performance of CODI’s continuing subsidiaries across periods.

Adjusted EBITDA attributable to the divested Sterno Food Service Business is calculated from Rimports’ reported results by identifying the net sales and directly attributable expenses of the Food Service Business and applying CODI’s Adjusted EBITDA methodology. Rimports and the Food Service Business historically operated and were reported together as Sterno Group under a shared management structure. Following the sale, certain shared management and other indirect costs remained with Rimports. Those costs remain in Rimports' results for all periods presented. Therefore, the exclusion of the Food Service Business does not eliminate all costs historically shared by the combined operations.

SYDNEY, Australia, Nov. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- GMEX Robotics Corporation (Nasdaq: GMEX) (the “Company”), today announced that it will effect a share consolidation of all of its issued and unissued existing Class A ordinary shares, Class B ordinary shares and Class C ordinary shares, of US$0.000001 par value each, at a ratio of 1-for-19, into one Class A, Class B and class C ordinary share of US$0.000019 par value, effective on November 27, 2026 (the “Share Consolidation”).

The Company’s Class A ordinary shares are expected to begin trading on a post-consolidation basis at the open of the market session on November 27, 2026. Upon the market opening on November 27, 2026, the Company’s Class A ordinary shares will continue to be traded on The Nasdaq Capital Market under the symbol “GMEX” with the new CUSIP number G3514S195. This decision represents a deliberate capital structure optimization, aligning the Company’s market profile with its significant operational progress and ambitious future roadmap.

The Share Consolidation was approved by the Company’s board of directors on October 23, 2026. Pursuant to the BVI Business Companies Act (as amended) and the Company’s Memorandum and Articles of Association, the Company’s Board of Directors is authorized to effect the Share Consolidation without the approval of the Company’s shareholders. Accordingly, no shareholder vote, consent or approval is required or will be sought in respect of the Share Consolidation.

As of November 11, 2026, there were 12,758,674 of the Company’s Class A ordinary shares outstanding and 89 Class B ordinary shares outstanding. Effecting the 1-for-19 Share Consolidation will reduce the outstanding Class A ordinary shares to 671,510 and the outstanding Class B ordinary shares to 5, subject to adjustment resulting from the treatment of fractional shares. There are no Class C ordinary shares outstanding as of November 11, 2026.

As a result of the Share Consolidation, the Company is authorised to issue a maximum of 1,368,421,072 shares of US$0.000019 par value each divided into: (i) 947,368,432 Class A ordinary shares of US$0.000019 par value each; (ii) 210,526,320 Class B ordinary shares of US$0.000019 par value each; and (iii) 210,526,320 Class C ordinary shares of US$0.000019 par value each.

“We are building a company designed for scale, performance, and sustained value creation,” stated Sam Lu, Chief Executive Officer of GMEX Robotics Corporation. “Our strengthened equity profile provides greater flexibility and a more robust platform for future value-accretive initiatives. This positions us optimally to consider strategic partnerships, acquisitions, or other capital market activities from a position of strength”.

As a result of the Share Consolidation, every nineteen (19) issued and unissued shares of each class of the Company’s shares will be automatically consolidated into one (1) share of the same class.

Outstanding warrants and other outstanding equity rights will be proportionately adjusted to reflect the Share Consolidation. No fractional shares will be issued in connection with the Share Consolidation, and in the event that a shareholder would otherwise be entitled to receive a fractional share upon the Share Consolidation, the number of shares to be received by such shareholder will be rounded up to one ordinary share of the same class in lieu of the fractional share that would have resulted from the Share Consolidation. Shareholders who are holding their shares in electronic form at brokerage firms do not need to take any action, as the effect of the Share Consolidation will automatically be reflected in their brokerage accounts.

The Company’s transfer agent, Vstock Transfer LLC, which is also acting as the exchange agent for the Share Consolidation, will send instructions to shareholders of record who hold stock certificates regarding the exchange of their old certificates for new certificates, should they wish to do so. Shareholders who hold their shares in brokerage accounts or “street name” are not required to take action to implement the exchange of their shares.

About GMEX Robotics:

Formerly known as Fitell Corporation, GMEX Robotics is a technology company operating at the intersection of consumer health and advanced automation. Building on a foundation of fitness equipment e-commerce, the Company is expanding its mission to design and deliver AI-driven robotic solutions that prioritize genuine consumer needs.

SANTA CLARA, Calif., Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Tuya Inc. ("Tuya" or the "Company") (NYSE: TUYA; HKEX: 2391), a global leading AI cloud platform service provider, today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026 and the declaration of a cash dividend.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights

  • Total revenue was US$98.6 million, up approximately 19.5% year-over-year (3Q2025: US$82.5 million).

  • Platform-as-a-service ("PaaS") revenue was US$70.1 million, up approximately 18.3% year-over-year (3Q2025: US$59.2 million).

  • AI application & others revenue was US$13.6 million, up approximately 18.6% year-over-year (3Q2025: US$11.5 million).

  • Smart home & robot product revenue was US$15.0 million, up approximately 26.7% year-over-year (3Q2025: US$11.8 million).

  • Overall gross margin was 45.8%, down 2.5 percentage points year-over-year (3Q2025: 48.3%). Gross margin of PaaS was 45.7% (3Q2025: 48.8%).

  • Operating margin was 9.0%, up 4.4 percentage points year-over-year (3Q2025: 4.6%). Non-GAAP operating margin was 9.5% (3Q2025: 10.8%).

  • Net margin was 18.8%, improved by 0.6 percentage points year-over-year (3Q2025: 18.2%). Non-GAAP net margin was 19.3% (3Q2025: 24.4%).

  • Net profit was US$18.5 million (3Q2025: US$15.0 million). Non-GAAP net profit was US$19.1 million (3Q2025: US$20.1 million).

  • Net cash generated from operating activities was US$12.7 million (3Q2025: US$30.0 million).

  • Total cash and cash equivalents, time deposits and treasury securities recorded as short-term and long-term investments were US$971.9 million as of September 30, 2026, compared to US$1,017.3 million as of December 31, 2025.

For further information on the non-GAAP financial measures presented above, see the section headed "Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures."

Third Quarter 2026 Operating Highlights

  • Premium PaaS customers[1] for the trailing 12 months ended September 30, 2026 were 331 (3Q2025: 280). In the third quarter of 2026, the Company's premium PaaS customers contributed approximately 89.6% of its PaaS revenue (3Q2025: approximately 88.0%).

  • Registered AI developers were over 2,180,000 as of September 30, 2026, up approximately 21.0% from approximately 1,801,000 developers as of December 31, 2025.
  1. The Company defines a premium PaaS customer as a customer as of a given date that contributed more than US$100,000 of PaaS revenue during the immediately preceding 12-month period.

Mr. Xueji (Jerry) Wang, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Tuya, commented, "In the third quarter, opportunities and challenges coexisted in the global consumer electronics industry. On the one hand, AI-native hardware continued to move from concept toward deployment at scale. New categories such as companion robots and AI toys rose rapidly, becoming a new engine for industry growth, which fully demonstrated that users' new demands for hardware in the AI era have begun to emerge. On the other hand, upstream component costs such as memory chips were still rising, and demand in traditional categories also faced pressure. Against this backdrop, we still maintained solid growth, with total revenue increasing by 19.5% year over year to US$98.6 million. The growth rate further accelerated compared to the second quarter, and we achieved year-over-year growth for the 13th consecutive quarter. In particular, PaaS revenue grew by 18.3% year over year, reflecting the continued increase in penetration of smart products across different regions and categories.

We continued to fully embrace AI and accelerated the promotion of ecosystem deployment. During the quarter, shipments of new AI-native categories grew by over 400% year over year. We debuted the AI home companion robot Doova at IFA in Berlin and the Global Digital Trade Expo. With the AI life assistant Hey Tuya as a core entry point, we integrated the three major application ecosystems of AI Home, AI Robot, and AI Energy, as well as the full-stack Matter combo solution. At the same time, subscription businesses such as door lock value-added services and pet cloud storage developed steadily, driving a continuous increase in the proportion of recurring revenue. Regarding developer tools, following Tuya Cobuilder, we launched the AI-native no-code application development platform Tuya AI Coding this quarter, extending developer tools from hardware development to application development. Looking ahead, we will focus on the three major scenarios mentioned above to promote large-scale shipments and the commercialization of AI-native hardware such as companion robots, pet care devices, and home energy management devices, and continue to improve the developer toolchain, Agent orchestration, and commercialization capabilities."

Mr. Yi (Alex) Yang, Director and Chief Financial Officer of Tuya, added, "In the third quarter, all three business segments delivered year-over-year revenue growth, with total revenue increasing by 19.5% year over year to US$98.6 million. As a foundation for our growth, the PaaS business saw its revenue increase by 18.3% year over year to US$70.1 million; Premium PaaS customers contributed approximately 89.6% of the PaaS revenue, and the core customer base remained stable. Smart home & robot product revenue grew by 26.7% year over year to US$15.0 million, primarily benefiting from growth in demand for categories such as AI audio and video, AI companion toys, and energy. AI application & others revenue increased by 18.6% year over year to US$13.6 million, primarily driven by the growth in cloud services, AI video cloud storage, and AI value-added services."

Third Quarter 2026 Unaudited Financial Results

REVENUE

Total revenue in the third quarter of 2026 increased by 19.5% to US$98.6 million from US$82.5 million in the same period of 2025.

  • PaaS revenue in the third quarter of 2026 increased by 18.3% to US$70.1 million from US$59.2 million in the same period of 2025, primarily due to increasing demand compared with the same period of 2025 and the Company's strategic focus on customer needs and product enhancements, despite the disruptions in the international business environment due to tariff-related headwinds since April 2025. Our core customer base remained stable.

  • AI application & others revenue in the third quarter of 2026 increased by 18.6% to US$13.6 million from US$11.5 million in the same period of 2025, primarily due to an increase in revenue from cloud-based services. During the quarter, the Company remained committed to offering recurring value-added services with AI application functions.

  • Smart home & robot product revenue in the third quarter of 2026 increased by 26.7% to US$15.0 million from US$11.8 million in the same period of 2025, primarily due to growing customer demands.

GROSS PROFIT AND GROSS MARGIN

Total gross profit in the third quarter of 2026 increased by 13.6% to US$45.2 million from US$39.8 million in the same period of 2025. The gross margin in the third quarter of 2026 was 45.8%, compared to 48.3% in the same period of 2025.

  • PaaS gross margin in the third quarter of 2026 was 45.7%, compared to 48.8% in the same period of 2025, partly attributable to recent price fluctuations in the semiconductor supply chain.

  • AI application & others gross margin in the third quarter of 2026 was 75.7%, compared to 70.8% in the same period of 2025.

  • Smart home & robot product gross margin in the third quarter of 2026 was 19.3%, compared to 23.8% in the same period of 2025.

Gross margin fluctuated primarily due to changes in product and solution mix, as well as fluctuations in semiconductor supply-chain pricing. As an AI developer platform with a rich ecosystem of smart devices and applications, the Company remains focused on AI offering with compelling value propositions while maintaining economic efficiency.

OPERATING EXPENSES

Operating expenses increased by 0.8% to US$36.3 million in the third quarter of 2026 from US$36.0 million in the same period of 2025. Non-GAAP operating expenses increased by 15.9% to US$35.8 million in the third quarter of 2026 from US$30.9 million in the same period of 2025. For further information on the non-GAAP financial measures presented above, see the section headed "Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures."

  • Research and development expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were US$25.0 million, up 9.7% from US$22.8 million in the same period of 2025, primarily due to i) higher employee-related cost and outsourced labor cost of US$1.8 million, ii) higher third-party cloud service fees of US$0.4 million, iii) partially offset by lower share-based compensation expenses of US$0.8 million as equity incentive awards granted at higher valuations in previous years have been gradually amortized. Non-GAAP adjusted research and development expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were US$24.6 million, compared to US$21.7 million in the same period of 2025.

  • Sales and marketing expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were US$9.3 million, up 16.9% from US$8.0 million in the same period of 2025, primarily because of i) higher employee-related cost of US$0.9 million, ii) higher third-party cloud expense of US$0.2 million, iii) partially offset by lower share-based compensation expenses of US$0.4 million as equity incentive awards granted at higher valuations in previous years have been gradually amortized. Non-GAAP adjusted sales and marketing expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were US$9.3 million, compared to US$7.5 million in the same period of 2025.

  • General and administrative expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were US$5.3 million, down 38.0% from US$8.5 million in the same period of 2025, primarily due to i) lower share-based compensation expenses of US$3.4 million as equity incentive awards granted at higher valuations in previous years have been gradually amortized, ii) partially offset by higher employee-related cost of US$0.3 million. Non-GAAP adjusted general and administrative expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were US$5.1 million, compared to US$4.9 million in the same period of 2025.

  • Other operating incomes, net in the third quarter of 2026 was US$3.3 million, primarily due to the receipt of software value-added tax refunds.

PROFIT FROM OPERATIONS AND OPERATING MARGIN

Profit from operations in the third quarter of 2026 was US$8.9 million, compared to US$3.8 million in the same period of 2025. The Company had a non-GAAP profit from operations of US$9.4 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to US$8.9 million in the same period of 2025, demonstrating consistent operating profitability and leverage.

Operating margin in the third quarter of 2026 was 9.0%, up 4.4 percentage points from 4.6% in the same period of 2025. Non-GAAP operating margin in the third quarter of 2026 was 9.5%, down 1.3 percentage points from 10.8% in the same period of 2025.

NET PROFIT AND NET MARGIN

Net profit in the third quarter of 2026 was US$18.5 million, an increase of 23.8% from US$15.0 million in the same period of 2025. Non-GAAP net profit in the third quarter of 2026 was US$19.1 million, compared to US$20.1 million in the same period of 2025.

Net margin in the third quarter of 2026 was 18.8%, an improvement of 0.6 percentage points from 18.2% in the same period of 2025. Non-GAAP net margin in the third quarter of 2026 was 19.3%, compared to 24.4% in the same period of 2025.

BASIC AND DILUTED NET PROFIT PER ADS

Basic and diluted net profit per ADS was US$0.03 in the third quarter of 2026, compared to US$0.02 in the same period of 2025. Each ADS represents one Class A ordinary share.

Non-GAAP basic and diluted net profit per ADS was US$0.03 in the third quarter of 2026, compared to US$0.03 in the same period of 2025.

CASH AND CASH EQUIVALENTS, TIME DEPOSITS AND TREASURY SECURITIES RECORDED AS SHORT-TERM AND LONG-TERM INVESTMENTS

Cash and cash equivalents, time deposits and treasury securities recorded as short-term and long-term investments were US$971.9 million as of September 30, 2026, compared to US$1,017.3 million as of December 31, 2025. The Company believes its current cash position is sufficient to meet its current liquidity and working capital needs.

NET CASH GENERATED FROM OPERATING ACTIVITIES

Net cash generated from operating activities in the third quarter of 2026 was US$12.7 million, compared to US$30.0 million in the same period of 2025. The net cash generated from operating activities for the third quarter of 2026 was mainly attributable to working capital changes in the ordinary course of business.

For further information on non-GAAP financial measures presented above, see the section headed "Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures."

Business Outlook

Currently, innovative AI hardware is in a rapid ramp-up phase, but the overall macroeconomic environment remains complex. On the one hand, AI-native hardware is moving from concept toward deployment at scale, with new categories such as companion robots and AI toys rising rapidly, becoming a new engine for industry growth. On the other hand, upstream component costs such as memory chips continue to rise, demand recovery in certain traditional categories is relatively slow, and uncertainties relating to trade policies and supply chains remain. Performance varies across regions, categories and markets. With the accelerated integration of AI and consumer hardware, Physical AI scenarios are ushering in a broader space for development.

Against this backdrop, we will continue to advance our AI-driven strategy. At the product level, we will focus on three high-potential scenarios, namely AI Home, AI Energy and AI Robot, to promote large-scale shipments and the commercialization of AI-native hardware such as companion robots, home energy management devices, and pet care devices. At the developer platform level, we will continue to improve Tuya Cobuilder, Tuya AI Coding and Agent orchestration capabilities, further lowering the development threshold, and enabling more customers and brands to quickly launch their own AI applications based on the Tuya platform. At the user application level, we will continue to enhance the response efficiency and reliability of Hey Tuya, and advance subscription and value-added services such as AI-powered protection, AI energy saving, pet care, and video understanding, to enhance our renewal and ongoing service capabilities.

Looking ahead, we will maintain disciplined execution, and continuously invest in AI R&D and platform capabilities. We will focus on AI-native applications, Physical AI scenarios, and developer platform construction, leveraging the advantages of our platform, device ecosystem and global developer base to transform AI technology from a tool capability into real and scalable commercial value. At the same time, we also recognize that our future performance may be affected by changes in consumer demand, regional economic conditions, inventory cycles, component and logistics costs, foreign exchange and interest-rate volatility, tariffs and trade-policy adjustments, and broader geopolitical uncertainties.

Declaration of Cash Dividend and Record Date

On November 23, 2026, the Board approved the declaration and distribution of a cash dividend (the "Cash Dividend") of US$0.0570 per ordinary share, or US$0.0570 per ADS, to such holders as at the close of business on January 6, 2027, Hong Kong Time and New York Time, respectively. The aggregate amount of the Cash Dividend will be approximately US$35 million, which is payable in U.S. dollars and in cash, and will be funded by surplus cash and to be paid out from the share premium account of the Company. The determination to make distributions and the amount of such distributions will be made at the discretion of its Board and will be based upon the Company's operations and earnings, including, but not limited to, considerations of the Company's GAAP and Non-GAAP net profits, cash flows, financial conditions and other relevant factors.

About Tuya Inc.

Tuya Inc. (NYSE: TUYA; HKEX: 2391) is a global leading AI cloud platform service provider with a mission to build an AI developer ecosystem and enable everything to be smart. 2026 Holiday Lineup Includes Santa Visits on Select Dates Dec. 4 – 20, Seasonal Lightings, a Radio City Rockettes Combo Ticket, and Festive Décor

NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--The Empire State Building (ESB), the "World's Most Famous Building," today announced its 2026 holiday celebrations, with festive décor throughout the iconic Observation Deck Experience, a Radio City Rockettes combo ticket, visits from Santa Claus, and screenings of “Home Alone 2: Lost in New York” and “Elf." Movie nights will take place on select dates Dec. 11 – 19 and Santa will visit on select dates Dec. 4 – 20. The seasonal lineup invites New Yorkers and visitors to celebrate the holidays at the #1 Top Attraction in the United States in Tripadvisor’s 2026 Travelers’ Choice Awards: Best of the Best Things to Do.

Santa Claus on the 86th Floor Observation Deck

“There is no better place for holiday activities in NYC than the Empire State Building, where the traditions of the season meet an authentic New York experience,” said Andrew Giancamilli, president of the Empire State Building Observation Deck and brand management. “From our festive décor and holiday movie nights to our world-famous views, we invite guests to celebrate the season at a place that is part of New York’s history and so many visitors’ holiday memories.”

All Dressed Up for the Holidays

Guests can pair skyline views with nearby gift shopping, seasonal treats, and beloved New York City holiday traditions.

NORWALK, Conn., Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Terex Corporation (NYSE: TEX) ("Terex") today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to sell its Aerials segment, including the Genie® brand, to Linamar Corporation (TSX: LNR) ("Linamar") for approximately $1.4 billion in cash, subject to customary adjustments.

The Aerials segment designs, manufactures, services and markets aerial work platform equipment and telehandlers as well as their related components and replacement parts sold under the Genie® brand. The transaction includes all assets of the business, including intellectual property, manufacturing footprint and parts and service operations.

The sale is the latest step in Terex's strategic transformation, which has included the 2024 acquisition of the Environmental Solutions Group, the 2025 exit of its Tower and Rough Terrain Cranes businesses, and the merger with REV Group, completed on February 2, 2026. Following the closing of the transaction, Terex will operate three segments: Environmental Solutions, Materials Processing and Specialty Vehicles.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, these three segments generated net sales of approximately $4.3 billion and segment Adjusted EBITDA of approximately $711 million, at a combined Adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 16.4% before corporate costs. Year to date Adjusted EBITDA margins were 17.0% for Environmental Solutions, 17.8% for Materials Processing and 15.0% for Specialty Vehicles.

Simon Meester, President and Chief Executive Officer of Terex, commented:

"This agreement is the result of a thorough strategic review of Aerials and delivers on the plan we previously announced, continuing the transformation of our portfolio from cyclical mining and construction markets to a leading position in resilient essential services markets. With this sale, Terex becomes a high mix, low volume specialty equipment manufacturer with steady replacement demand, low capital intensity and strong conversion of earnings into free cash flow. That gives us greater flexibility to invest in the business and deliver more predictable and accretive returns to shareholders over time. Genie has a talented team with a respected position across its markets, and Linamar is a strong long-term owner for the business, its customers and its employees. I want to thank the Aerials team for their contributions to Terex and for their continued commitment through the transition ahead."

Strategic Positioning

  • Leading Specialty Equipment Portfolio. Terex will concentrate on businesses with strong brands serving the emergency vehicle market, waste collection, utilities, infrastructure, recycling and materials processing, with strong synergies across the portfolio.
  • Shift in Mix Toward Low Cyclical Essential Services. Excluding Aerials, first nine months 2026 net sales were approximately 40% Specialty Vehicles (public safety and recreation), 30% Environmental Solutions (waste and utilities) and 30% Materials Processing (infrastructure and recycling).
  • Steady Replacement Demand and $6.2B Backlog ex-Aerials. Terex's businesses serve end markets characterized by steady replacement demand and long-term growth, supported by an extensive manufacturing footprint, primarily within the U.S., and strong backlog providing forward demand planning visibility.
  • Low Capital Intensity and Strong Cash Flow Conversion. The continuing businesses are expected to combine low capital intensity with durable, predictable earnings, driving strong free cash flow conversion.

Transaction Details

Under the terms of the agreement, which has been unanimously approved by the Terex Board of Directors, Linamar will acquire Terex's Aerials business, including the Genie® brand, intellectual property, manufacturing footprint and parts and service operations, for approximately $1.4 billion in cash, subject to customary adjustments. The transaction is expected to close in 2027, subject to the receipt of required regulatory approvals and the satisfaction of other customary closing conditions.

Advisors

UBS Investment Bank and Barclays Capital are serving as financial advisors to Terex, and Fried, Frank, Harris, Shriver & Jacobson LLP is serving as legal counsel.

About Terex

Terex Corporation is a global leader in specialized equipment solutions, serving essential sectors such as emergency services, waste and recycling, utilities, and construction. Our diversified portfolio positions us in resilient, high-demand markets with strong long-term growth potential.

We design and manufacture advanced specialty vehicles—including fire, ambulance, and recreational vehicles—alongside waste collection vehicles, materials processing machinery, mobile elevating work platforms, and equipment for the electric utility industry. Through our global dealer, parts and service network and true value-creating digital solutions, we deliver best-in-class lifecycle support, helping customers maximize return on investment.

With its center of gravity firmly in the United States, anchored by a strong domestic manufacturing footprint and complemented by operations across Europe and Asia Pacific, Terex combines local expertise with global reach to capture opportunities worldwide. Our strategy is clear: exceed customer expectations, invest in innovation, leverage our diversified portfolio, and deliver consistent, profitable growth for our shareholders.
